theme: FGF receptor activation and downstream signalling, including oncogenic FGFR mutants
story: The centre is FGF ligand binding to the splice-variant receptors FGFR1-4 (IIIb/IIIc isoforms, set by FGFR2 alternative splicing) and the adaptor cascades they trigger: FRS2-, SHC-, PLC-gamma- and PI3K-mediated signalling. Around this core sit the disease forms of the same receptors: activating point mutants, amplifications, the t(4;14) FGFR3 translocation of myeloma and FGFR4 mutants, which drive the same cascades constitutively, plus FGFRL1 as a decoy-like modulator. As a whole the cluster describes how FGFR tyrosine kinases relay growth-factor signals into RAS/MAPK, PI3K and calcium pathways, and how cancers hijack that relay.

theme: Heme biosynthesis and mitochondrial iron-cofactor supply
story: The core is the heme biosynthetic route through protoporphyrinogen IX to heme B and heme A, with regulation of tetrapyrrole metabolism and of hemoglobin synthesis tying it to erythroid demand (the hallmark heme metabolism set). Mitochondrial ABC transporters (such as ABCB7 and ABCB10) and cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly are the iron-handling partners: they export the precursors and Fe-S intermediates that heme and Fe-S cofactor production depend on. Together the cluster describes how mitochondria build iron-containing cofactors, chiefly heme for hemoglobin and respiratory cytochromes.

theme: Axon guidance by repulsive cues and axon regeneration/sprouting
story: The centre is repulsive axon guidance: Sema3A-plexin signalling via CRMPs, PAK and integrin inhibition, netrin repulsion, and Eph-A-driven growth cone collapse, which act on the microtubule and actin cytoskeleton to stop or turn axon extension. The same machinery is reused after injury, so the cluster also holds positive and negative regulation of axon regeneration, injured-axon sprouting and collateral sprouting, with fasciculation, nerve branching, DRG development and motor neuron survival as developmental contexts. Overall it describes how growth cones read guidance cues to steer, bundle, branch and regrow axons.

theme: Nucleotide-sugar supply and N-glycan processing, with CDG disorders
story: The core is getting activated sugar donors (UDP-glucose, UDP-GlcNAc, UDP-glucuronate, CMP-sialic acid, GDP-fucose, dolichyl-phosphate-glucose) into the ER and Golgi via SLC35-family nucleotide-sugar transporters and the acetyl-CoA transporter SLC33A1. These donors feed N-linked glycosylation and N-glycan trimming (MOGS, MAN1B1), and lysosomal oligosaccharide catabolism is the degradative end of the same glycans; most members are the congenital disorders of glycosylation caused when a transporter or trimming enzyme fails. The cluster as a whole describes the supply and processing line of N-glycosylation in the secretory pathway and the diseases of its breakdown.

theme: Hormonal control of hepatic glucose and lipid fuel balance
story: The centre is the switch between gluconeogenesis and glycolysis: glucagon-driven PKA activation phosphorylates key metabolic factors and alters fructose-2,6-bisphosphate levels, flipping liver flux toward glucose output, with positive and negative regulation of gluconeogenesis on both sides. AMPK inhibition of ChREBP, LXR (NR1H2/NR1H3) control of gluconeogenic genes, and regulation of triglyceride synthesis, fatty acid homeostasis and adipose development connect the same nutrient-sensing signals to lipogenesis and fat storage, with caloric restriction as a physiological trigger. Overall the cluster describes how fed/fasted hormonal and energy signals allocate fuel between glucose production and fat storage.

theme: Glial myelination and axon maintenance, injury and regeneration
story: The core is myelin: Schwann cell myelination initiated by EGR2 and SOX10, CNS and PNS myelin formation and maintenance, oligodendrocyte progenitor proliferation, negative regulation of myelination and LGI-ADAM interactions at the axon-glia junction. Axonal partners include neurofilament organisation and axon diameter control, which myelin depends on and influences, while axon regeneration, injured-axon sprouting, reactive gliosis and astrocyte migration describe the response of axons and glia to nerve damage. Together the cluster depicts the axon-glia unit: how glia wrap and sustain axons and how both respond to injury.

theme: Embryonic kidney development from intermediate mesoderm to nephrons
story: The cluster follows nephrogenesis from intermediate mesoderm and nephric duct formation, through pronephros and metanephros, to ureteric bud elongation and reciprocal induction of the metanephric mesenchyme. The centre is mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition forming renal vesicles and tubules, with proximal/distal patterning and tubule epithelial differentiation, while maintenance of nephron progenitor stem cells and suppression of mesenchymal apoptosis keep the progenitor pool alive. As a whole it describes how the kidney builds its nephrons during development.

theme: Heavy-metal sensing and detoxification via MTF1 and metallothioneins
story: The centre is the metal-responsive transcription factor MTF1 inducing metallothioneins, which bind and sequester zinc, copper, cadmium and mercury. The cellular responses to individual metal ions and cadmium transport and detoxification are the inputs and the context this system handles. Overall the cluster describes how cells sense excess or toxic metal ions and buffer them to protect against heavy-metal toxicity.

theme: Renin-angiotensin regulation of blood pressure and fluid volume
story: The core is the renin-angiotensin system: angiotensinogen processing to angiotensins, control of angiotensin levels, angiotensin receptor signalling, and renin-angiotensin regulation of blood volume and renal blood flow. Peptidase activities (ACE-type catabolism of bradykinin and neuropeptides), renal sodium excretion and urine volume, nervous-system and epinephrine contributions to arterial pressure, and drinking behaviour are the effector and parallel arms. Together the cluster describes the integrated hormonal, renal, neural and behavioural control of systemic blood pressure and body fluid volume.

theme: Sulfur amino acid catabolism and selenium metabolism
story: The centre is the transsulfuration pathway, in which homocysteine and serine are converted to cysteine by cystathionine beta-synthase and cystathionine gamma-lyase, together with downstream catabolism of cysteine and other sulfur amino acids. Selenium compounds (selenomethionine, selenocysteine, selenate/selenite, methylseleninic acid) are processed by the same enzymes into hydrogen selenide and then methylated for excretion, because selenium chemically mimics sulfur. As a whole the cluster describes how the transsulfuration enzymes handle sulfur and its selenium analogues.

theme: Innate antiviral sensing and type I interferon response
story: The centre is cytosolic nucleic acid sensing by RIG-I/MDA5 (DDX58/IFIH1) and DNA sensors, which signal through TRAF3/TRAF6 to IRF3/IRF7 and NF-kB to induce type I interferon, with negative regulators and OTU deubiquitinases tuning the pathway. Downstream, interferon-alpha responses and interferon-stimulated genes (ISG15 conjugation, OAS, IP-10) carry out antiviral effector functions, captured also by dendritic cell activation and IFN signature modules, while RSV and SARS-CoV entries show viruses evading or modulating this system. Overall the cluster describes the full arc from virus detection to interferon production and the antiviral state.

theme: Type 2 (Th2) immunity: IL-4, IL-5, IL-13 and IL-33
story: The centre is Th2 cell differentiation and its signature cytokines IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, with both positive and negative regulation of their production and IL-4/IL-13 receptor signalling. IL-33 signalling acts as an upstream alarmin that drives type 2 responses, mast cell cytokine production is an innate source of the same cytokines, and IgE isotype switching is the B cell outcome. Together the cluster describes the type 2 immune axis underlying allergy and anti-helminth defence.

theme: NOTCH receptor signalling to the nucleus and its oncogenic activation
story: The core is canonical Notch signalling: NOTCH1-4 activation, cleavage and nuclear translocation of the intracellular domain, which drives HES/HEY (HLH) target transcription, plus positive and negative regulators such as RUNX3. Constitutive NOTCH1 mutants (HD, PEST, translocation) and FBXW7 loss, which stabilises the NOTCH1 intracellular domain, are the cancer forms of the same pathway, notably in T-ALL. As a whole the cluster describes Notch signal transmission and its dysregulation in disease.

theme: Surface marker signatures of immune cell types
story: These are blood transcriptional modules and surface signatures defining leukocyte identities: monocytes, resting and activated dendritic cells, naive and total B cells, and T cells. Antigen-presentation and myeloid receptor/transporter modules capture the shared surface machinery (MHC, receptors) these cells display. The cluster as a whole is a cell-type marker panel used to read immune cell composition from expression data rather than a single biological process.

theme: TRKA neurotrophin signalling to MAPK, PI3K and CREB
story: The centre is NGF-activated TRKA signalling through FRS2 and ARMS adaptors to RAS, RIT/RIN and the ERK, ERK5 and p38 MAPK cascades. These converge on CREB phosphorylation and NGF-stimulated transcription, with PI3K/AKT providing survival signalling; MAP2K mutants and positive regulation of Ras signalling represent the shared MAPK core. Overall the cluster describes how neurotrophin receptor activation is relayed to gene expression for neuronal survival and differentiation.

theme: Antigen processing and presentation via MHC class II and CD1
story: The centre is the MHC class II pathway: exogenous peptide processing, peptide loading onto MHC II, and its positive and negative regulation, including in germinal centre B cells. CD1-mediated lipid antigen presentation extends this to lipids, while antigen-presentation and monocyte expression modules and the MHC-TLR7/8 cluster tie it to the professional antigen-presenting cells that couple endosomal sensing with presentation. Together the cluster describes how APCs process and display antigens to T cells.

theme: Early embryonic axis patterning, neural plate and hindbrain segmentation
story: The centre is body-plan patterning: dorsal/ventral axis specification, anterior and posterior neural plate formation, neural plate border and neural crest specification, and hindbrain segmentation into rhombomeres with anterior HOX gene activation and midbrain-hindbrain boundary formation. Limb and digit morphogenesis and thorax/abdomen determination apply the same positional signalling (HOX, morphogen gradients) to other axes, and boundary formation and signal-driven gene expression are the general mechanisms. As a whole the cluster describes how morphogen and HOX codes establish positional identity in the early embryo.

theme: Neurotrophin signalling: TRK survival versus p75NTR death
story: The cluster centres on neurotrophin receptor signalling, split into two arms: TRKA-driven survival and growth (FRS2/ARMS, ERK5, p38, PI3K/AKT, CREB, NGF-stimulated transcription, axonal growth) and p75NTR signalling, where proNGF binding, regulated proteolysis and adaptors (NRIF, NRAGE, NADE, ceramide, NF-kB) decide between death and survival. Dependence receptor behaviour (NTRK3, caspase activation without ligand), NGF production and processing, and regulation of neuron maturation and glial apoptosis complete the picture. Overall it describes how neurotrophins determine neuron survival, growth or apoptosis.

theme: Golgi organisation and COPI vesicle trafficking
story: The centre is the Golgi as a dynamic organelle: COPI vesicle budding mediating retrograde Golgi-to-ER and intra-Golgi transport, plus anterograde secretory flow, vesicle tethering and fusion, and Golgi protein retention. Golgi structural dynamics, including ribbon formation, disassembly and reassembly during mitosis, pericentriolar stacking and localisation, and membrane tubulation, are the other half. Together the cluster describes how the Golgi maintains its architecture and moves cargo through the secretory pathway.

theme: p53 and p14ARF control of DNA damage, apoptosis, cell cycle
story: The centre is TP53 control: its phosphorylation and MDM2/COP1-mediated degradation, its transcription of DNA repair genes and its induction of intrinsic apoptosis after DNA damage. p14ARF defects and p53 loss-of-function mutants are the cancer side, enabling escape from apoptosis and from oncogene- or stress-induced senescence, while G2/M checkpoint elements (GTSE1, Cdc25A degradation, MASTL, cell cycle module) connect p53 to cell cycle arrest and recovery. Overall the cluster describes the p53 tumour-suppressor network that decides between repair, arrest, senescence and death.

theme: Meiotic prophase I: recombination and synapsis in germ cells
story: The core is meiotic recombination: programmed double-strand break formation, their repair and resolution of recombination intermediates, coupled to synaptonemal complex assembly, homologue synapsis and telomere attachment to the nuclear envelope. Meiotic checkpoints and regulation of meiosis I entry and nuclear division control progression, in both male and female germ cells, with the spermatogenesis hallmark as the tissue context. Together the cluster describes how germ cells pair and recombine homologous chromosomes in the first meiotic division.

theme: Cellular and renal salt and water (osmotic) homeostasis
story: The centre is osmotic balance: cellular responses to hyperosmotic, hypotonic and salt stress, osmosensory signalling and intracellular water homeostasis. Renal sodium transport, aldosterone responses, regulated sodium import, transepithelial chloride transport and renin-angiotensin renal effects are the organism-level mechanisms that set extracellular salt and volume. Overall the cluster describes how cells and the kidney sense and correct salt and water imbalance.

theme: Lipoxygenase-derived lipid mediators and resolution of inflammation
story: The centre is the lipoxygenase pathway acting on arachidonic acid and omega-3 fatty acids (EPA, DHA, DPA) to produce HETEs, hepoxilins, lipoxins and the specialised pro-resolving mediators: resolvins, protectins, maresins and their tissue-regeneration conjugates, including aspirin-triggered forms. Arachidonate-derived pro-inflammatory metabolites and electrophilic oxo-derivatives sit alongside as the inflammatory counterpart. Together the cluster describes how oxygenated fatty acid mediators first drive and then actively resolve inflammation.

theme: Amino sugar and sialic acid metabolism and GPI anchor synthesis
story: The centre is the hexosamine pathway: fructose-6-phosphate conversion (GFPT1) to glucosamine and UDP-GlcNAc, with GlcNAc and mannose metabolism and amino sugar catabolism. UDP-GlcNAc feeds sialic acid synthesis (GNE, CMP-sialic acid) and the first step of GPI anchor synthesis, which is then attached to proteins such as uPAR; ALG14, GFPT1 and GNE defects are the disorders when this supply fails. Overall the cluster describes the production of amino sugar building blocks used for glycoconjugates and membrane anchors.

theme: Cellular senescence: arrest, Polycomb silencing and SASP
story: The centre is cellular senescence induced by oncogenes, oxidative stress and other stresses, with positive regulation of senescence and blocked G0-to-G1 re-entry. Polycomb chromatin silencing (BMI1, PRC1/PRC2) at the CDKN2A locus and AP-2 control of cell cycle genes decide whether cells keep cycling, while the senescence-associated secretory phenotype and stress-kinase regulation form the inflammatory output. Together the cluster describes how cells permanently exit proliferation and signal to their surroundings.

theme: Transport of carboxylates, pyruvate and carnitine for energy metabolism
story: The centre is membrane transport of metabolic carboxylates: sodium-coupled di- and tricarboxylate carriers (succinate, alpha-ketoglutarate, citrate), proton-coupled monocarboxylate transport (pyruvate, lactate) and organic anion SLC transporters. Carnitine transport (with SLC22A5 deficiency) supplies fatty acid oxidation, pyruvate catabolism is the downstream use, and proximal tubule development reflects the kidney as a major site of such reabsorption. Overall the cluster describes how cells and the kidney move fuel intermediates across membranes.

theme: Regulation of Ras-ERK MAPK signalling
story: The centre is the Ras-to-ERK MAPK cascade with its positive and negative regulation, including RIT/RIN signalling to p38, MAP2K mutants and RSK activation downstream of ERK. Tyrosine dephosphorylation (MAPK phosphatases) and negative regulation of ERK1/2 provide the feedback that shuts the pathway off. Together the cluster describes the tuning of Ras-MAPK signal intensity and duration.

theme: Death receptor-driven apoptosis and necroptosis
story: The centre is extrinsic apoptosis via death receptors (FAS, TRAIL receptors): DISC formation, procaspase-8 dimerisation and BID cleavage linking to mitochondria, with c-FLIP and caspase-8 inhibition as brakes. When caspase-8 is blocked, RIPK1-dependent necroptosis takes over, and pathogens (including SARS-CoV-1) modulate both outcomes; TNF signalling regulation, hepatocyte apoptosis and tumour cell killing are contexts. Overall the cluster describes how death-receptor signals choose between apoptotic and necroptotic cell death.

theme: Fertilisation: sperm motility, capacitation and sperm-egg interaction
story: The centre is the sequence of fertilisation: sperm motility and chemotaxis, capacitation, passage through cumulus cells, binding to and penetration of the zona pellucida, the acrosome reaction and sperm-oocyte membrane fusion. Egg activation and positive and negative regulation of fertilisation complete the process, with cilium movement regulation reflecting the flagellar motor. Together the cluster describes how sperm reach and fertilise the egg.

theme: Growth factor-driven sprouting angiogenesis and endothelial activation
story: The centre is sprouting angiogenesis: VEGF production and VEGFR signalling driving endothelial cell proliferation, chemotaxis, migration, tube morphogenesis and vessel branching. FGF receptor signalling and TGF-beta2 production are co-stimulatory growth factor inputs, while endothelial activation, apoptosis and vascular wound healing round out endothelial behaviour, summarised by the angiogenesis hallmark. Overall the cluster describes how growth factors make endothelial cells build new blood vessels.

theme: Neuroendocrine regulation of sleep, arousal and stress behaviour
story: The centre is regulation of the sleep/wake cycle (REM, non-REM, wakefulness) and locomotor rhythm, with orexin and related neuropeptides as key arousal signals. Stress responses through CRH and corticosterone, fear, immobilisation stress and general adaptation link the same neuropeptide circuits to stress behaviour, while drinking, parental and ethanol-related behaviours reflect broader motivated behaviours they modulate. Overall the cluster describes neuropeptide and hormonal control of arousal state and stress-related behaviour.

theme: TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation with Fe-S cofactors
story: The centre is the tricarboxylic acid cycle (succinate and malate metabolism, enzyme maturation and regulation) linked to the respiratory chain through succinate dehydrogenase (complex II) and on to ATP synthase. Iron-sulfur cluster assembly ([2Fe-2S], [4Fe-4S]) supplies the cofactors required by aconitase, SDH and respiratory complexes. Together the cluster describes mitochondrial oxidative energy production and the Fe-S cofactors it depends on.

theme: MicroRNA biogenesis control in fibroblast activation and fibrosis
story: One centre is miRNA biogenesis: miRNA transcription and positive and negative regulation of primary and pre-miRNA processing. The other is fibrotic repair: myofibroblast and cardiac fibroblast differentiation, fibroblast apoptosis, TGF-beta responsiveness, extracellular matrix assembly and connective tissue replacement in wound healing. The cluster suggests miRNAs acting as regulators of TGF-beta-driven fibroblast activation and scarring, though the link is joined by shared regulators rather than one pathway.

theme: LDL receptor internalisation, degradation and cholesterol uptake
story: The centre is the LDL receptor family (LDLR, VLDLR) and LDL particle clearance, with regulators that promote receptor internalisation and lysosomal degradation and suppress recycling (as PCSK9 and IDOL do). LXR (NR1H2/NR1H3) induction of IDOL to limit cholesterol uptake and regulation of cholesterol import connect this to cellular sterol sensing. Overall the cluster describes how cells control lipoprotein receptor levels to regulate cholesterol uptake.

theme: Ubiquitin, deubiquitination and proteasome protein turnover
story: The centre is the ubiquitin code: E1/E2/E3 ubiquitination with diverse chain types (K6, K11, K27, K29, K48, K63, branched, free chains) and its removal by deubiquitinases (USP, UCH, OTU, metalloprotease DUBs). Proteasome assembly and ubiquitin-dependent and -independent degradation are the main output, while neddylation and the COP9 signalosome regulate cullin ligases (e.g. BTRC-CUL1 degradation of NFE2L2); sumoylation, de-ADP-ribosylation, Golgi reassembly and an RB1/BCL2L1 module are peripheral. Together the cluster describes the ubiquitin-proteasome system controlling protein fate.

theme: COPI vesicle targeting between ER and Golgi
story: The centre is COPI-coated vesicle budding and retrograde Golgi-to-ER transport. Vesicle targeting from rough ER to cis-Golgi and protein localisation to ER exit sites describe the anterograde half of the same shuttle. Overall the cluster describes vesicle traffic cycling between the ER and Golgi.

theme: Proteoglycan glycosaminoglycan synthesis, sulfation and degradation
story: The centre is glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis on proteoglycans: heparan sulfate (EXT1/EXT2), heparin and chondroitin sulfate biosynthesis. Sulfation supply is the key support: PAPS synthesis (PAPSS2), sulfate transport (SLC26A2), nucleotide-sugar transport (SLC35D1) and arylsulfatase activation, while hyaluronan degradation is the catabolic counterpart; many members are the skeletal dysplasias and exostoses from these defects. Together the cluster describes the making and sulfation of cartilage and extracellular matrix glycosaminoglycans.

theme: Integrated stress response and unfolded protein response
story: The centre is stress-induced control of translation through eIF2-alpha kinases: PERK in the UPR, HRI for heme deficiency and GCN2 for amino acid starvation, which shut down general translation while promoting stress-specific translation. The ER-stress branches (PERK, IRE1) with their positive and negative regulation, and ER stress-induced apoptosis including in pancreatic beta cells, describe the outcome when stress persists; ufmylation is an ER-associated modifier. Overall the cluster describes how cells sense protein-folding and nutrient stress and decide between adaptation and death.

theme: Kidney development and regulation of kidney growth
story: The cluster centres on the developmental series pronephros, mesonephros and metanephros, with nephric/mesonephric duct formation and metanephric tubule formation. The other members regulate growth: positive and negative control of kidney development and size, limiting cell proliferation, and maintaining nephron progenitor stem cells by blocking mesenchymal apoptosis. Together it describes how the kidney is built and how its final size is controlled.

theme: Type I interferon antiviral response signature
story: The centre is the type I interferon/interferon-alpha response and its antiviral effectors: ISG15 conjugation, OAS and IP-10 (CXCL10). Virus sensing, cytosolic DNA sensing and IRF2 target networks supply the upstream trigger, while the activated dendritic cell and antiviral IFN signature modules capture the same programme in blood expression data. Overall the cluster describes the interferon-stimulated antiviral state.

theme: Lysosomal catabolism of glycans and glycosphingolipids
story: The centre is the lysosome breaking down glycoconjugates: oligosaccharide and glycoside catabolism, glycosphingolipid and ganglioside degradation by hexosaminidases and neuraminidase, and amino sugar catabolism. Lysosomal protein modules and lysosomal enzyme secretion/targeting describe the organelle machinery, and the disease entries (HEXA/HEXB GM2 gangliosidoses, NEU1 sialidosis, MAN1B1) are the storage disorders when one step fails. Together the cluster describes lysosomal degradation of sugar-containing molecules.

theme: Nucleotide-sugar supply for glycosylation, GPI anchors and glycolipids
story: The centre is the production and Golgi import of nucleotide sugars: UDP-GlcNAc synthesis (GFPT1), sialic acid and CMP-sialic acid (GNE), UDP-glucose and UDP-glucuronate, plus SLC35 and SLC33A1 transport into the secretory pathway. These donors feed GPI anchor synthesis and attachment, glycosphingolipid, galactosylceramide and ganglioside biosynthesis, and protein glycosylation, and most named defects are congenital glycosylation disorders or myasthenic syndromes from this supply. Overall the cluster describes the sugar-donor supply that builds glycoproteins, GPI-anchored proteins and glycolipids.

theme: RNA modification, mainly mitochondrial tRNA processing and pseudouridylation
story: The centre is mitochondrial tRNA maturation: processing from polycistronic transcripts, 3'-end processing and base modification. Pseudouridine synthesis in tRNA, mRNA and rRNA adds the shared enzymatic chemistry (pseudouridine synthases such as PUS1 act in both mitochondria and cytosol). Together the cluster describes post-transcriptional RNA maturation and modification, especially for mitochondrial translation.

theme: cAMP second-messenger signalling to PKA and CREB
story: The centre is cAMP: its synthesis by adenylate cyclases activated by GPCRs such as dopamine and serotonin receptors and by calcium/calmodulin, and its breakdown by phosphodiesterases including calmodulin-dependent PDE1. Downstream, PKA signalling, DARPP-32 in dopaminoceptive neurons and CREB phosphorylation carry the signal to gene expression, with negative regulation of cAMP/PKA as feedback. Overall the cluster describes the neuronal cAMP-PKA-CREB second-messenger pathway.

theme: Leukotriene and eicosanoid biosynthesis, transport and catabolism
story: The centre is the 5-lipoxygenase route making leukotrienes (LTB4, LTC4/D4) and eoxins from arachidonic acid, alongside 5- and 15-HETE and lipoxin synthesis. Leukotriene transport, catabolism, eicosanoid omega-oxidation and ER lipid metabolism describe how these mediators are exported and inactivated, and LTC4-CysLT receptor-driven IL-4 production shows their immune effect. Together the cluster describes the life cycle of pro-inflammatory leukotriene signals.

theme: Axon guidance by netrin and SLIT-ROBO midline signalling
story: The centre is midline axon guidance: SLIT-ROBO repulsion and netrin attraction/repulsion steering commissural axons at the midline choice point. These receptors act on Rho GTPases (RAC1, CDC42, RHOA) and ABL/AKAP5 to remodel the growth cone, and the cluster includes guidance of specific tracts (corticospinal, dopaminergic, serotonergic) and regulation of ROBO/SLIT expression, with chemotaxis regulation as a parallel use of SLIT-ROBO in leukocytes. Overall it describes how growth cones navigate across and away from the midline.

theme: DNA double-strand break sensing and repair pathway choice
story: The centre is double-strand break repair: sensing by the MRN complex and ATM-mediated recruitment and phosphorylation of repair proteins. The rest are the competing repair routes, classical NHEJ, alternative end joining/MMEJ and homologous recombination including synthesis-dependent strand annealing, together with their positive and negative regulators. Together the cluster describes how cells detect DSBs and choose a repair pathway.

theme: Oocyte meiotic divisions: spindle, cohesion and chromosome segregation
story: The centre is female meiosis: meiotic spindle assembly and positioning, chromosome alignment, chiasma and centromeric cohesion, and segregation with polar body extrusion. Meiotic checkpoints and regulation of G2/MI, metaphase/anaphase transitions and separation time the divisions, with spermatogenesis and embryonic cleavage marking the germline and post-fertilisation context. Overall the cluster describes how oocytes accurately segregate chromosomes through meiosis.

theme: Amino sugar and sialic acid metabolism and lysosomal turnover
story: The centre is amino sugar metabolism: fructose-6-phosphate to GlcNAc, mannose and sialic acid synthesis (GNE, CMP-sialic acid), and the reverse catabolism of these sugars. The lysosomal arm degrades glycoconjugates and exports free sialic acid via SLC17A5 (Salla disease), with NEU1, HEXA and MAN1B1 defects as storage and glycosylation disorders. Together the cluster describes the synthesis and recycling of amino sugars and sialic acid.

theme: Actin filament dynamics in cell motility
story: The centre is actin filament turnover: polymerisation, depolymerisation, severing, barbed-end capping and Arp2/3 nucleation. Crosslinking and network formation build higher-order structures such as ruffles that power polymerisation-driven motility, while caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins dismantles them during apoptosis. Overall the cluster describes how the actin cytoskeleton is assembled, remodelled and taken apart to drive cell movement and shape.
